Review Title: Amazing views of the South Rim
Review Text:
This tour is worth every cent. We were picked up promptly from our hotel, then taken to the airfield. Checked in and boarded our small plane to fly out to the South Rim of the Grand Canyon. The weather was 45 degrees, so very hot, but they got flying quickly. Flew over the hoover dam and Lake Mead before arriving at the Canyon.

Then we were put into an open air hummer for a 2 hour tour. This was great, stopped at lots of lookouts, the guide took lots of photos. Given a delicious, fresh lunch to enjoy overlooking the south rim of the canyon.

After lunch we were taken to a heliport for a helicopter ride out to and over the canyon - breathtaking. Then flown back to Las Vegas in the light plane.

Only downside was upon checkin, they advised us that the price of fuel had increased so it would therefore be an extra $33pp - would have been nice to have been told beforehand, rather than right there on the spot - we couldn't back out, not that we would have, but given the price of this tour, I think some correspondence would have been nice.

Review Title: NOT TO BE MISSED, PANORAMA IS WORTH THE EXPENSE
Review Text:
Absolutely to book in advance because you can't do without it.
We booked it a few days before and called to confirm the reservation.
In June 2023 we spent 164 euros each for the flight + 14 euros each for fuel surcharge, it's a lot but the excursion is worth it all.
Having arrived at the airport half an hour early, there was a terrible wind blowing and we were asked if we still wanted to fly as there would have been strong turbulence and if we preferred to cancel they would refund the cost of the tickets.
We asked if we would fly safely, in which case we would have preferred to fly now we were there and we couldn't postpone it as it was an itinerant trip.
It shook so much that you risked crashing your camera into the window, every now and then several driving alarms began to sound and several warning lights came on.
The flight lasts about 40 minutes and was quite challenging and towards the end we had become quiet and a tried...
But I guarantee it was worth it, if I could go back I would do it again without a doubt and I highly recommend it.
From above you have the perception of the earth's crust and the crack that passes through it, it is a completely different image from the one you get when seeing the grand canyon from the various panoramic points on the edge.
I don't want to diminish the beauty of the grand canyon from the views, but in my opinion the flight completes the experience, absolutely worth the money spent.
The plane is honestly dated and the headphone supports and the regulators for the audio guide are now falling to pieces, a little more maintenance could be done on the internal instruments, but I realize that it will always be in flight and the time available is not much, but given the expense one would expect better maintained instruments.
Our flight had 8 seats and we all sat at the window.

Review Text:
We had originally thought about doing a helicopter trip of the Canyon, but several people who'd visited suggested the airplane tour was better. We decided to go for it and weren't disappointed.

We managed to book for 11am the following day which suited our schedule perfectly and arrived at their smart reception area at 10:20 as requested.

We were met by the pilot at 10:45 who showed us out to the waiting Cessna Grand Caravan. This is a perfect airplane for this type of trip since it is high-wing and affords an excellent view. Each of the comfortable seats was equipped with good-quality headsets so one could listen to the commentary throughout. The airplane was not too noisy, and it was still possible to hold a conversation with someone on the opposite side of the airplane (after removing the headset of course).

We were soon in the air and flying over the rim of the canyon. It takes a circular clockwise route and covers around 100 miles of the north and south sides of the canyon with excellent views including the Colorado river.

We returned for a very smooth landing around 40 minutes later.

Overall, this was an excellent experience at a reasonable price with plenty of opportunities to take great photos and videos. I would highly recommend it.

One minor gripe - we were asked to pay a $15 per person fuel surcharge at reception and I consider it would be better to incorporate this into the published price.

Review Title: This is the way to tour the Grand Canyon
Review Text:
Trip Reserved: Grand Canyon Deluxe with Hummer
Our Group: 2 families (4 adults, 2 teenage boys)

On a recent trip to Las Vegas, we wanted the views of the South Rim without the 9 hour round trip drive from Vegas. After some searching I found this tour. It's not inexpensive, so we considered it for a while before booking.

I had been to the grand canyon twice. My husband and son never had. My husband's initial take was to simply do the 2.5 hour drive from Vegas to the West Rim, proclaiming "rocks are rocks."

In the end, knowing that the south rim is much more spectacular, we ended up booking this trip. It's a full day, that started with pick up at our hotel, and transfer to the Boulder City airport west of LV. From there we boarded an 8 passenger plane for a flight over the Hoover Dam, and part of the Grand Canyon before landing at the Grand Canyon Airport. The flight was narrated. Not by the pilot... there were headphones available and a pre-recorded narration in a few languages. It wasn't fantastic, but I appreciated that there was some narration to what we were seeing, and I did learn from it.

Once we landed, we transferred to open-air hummers for a several hour tour through several different vantage points in Grand Canyon National Park. Our tour guide was fantastic. His love of the GC is evident and comes through in his delivery. We had a boxed lunch (turkey sandwich, apple, chips, cookie, water). He had some fun suggestions for photos. He was very willing to play the role of photographer and take photos. And he was so knowledgeable and just had so much enjoyment about sharing "his Grand Canyon with us"

We returned via the same plane and were dropped off back at our hotel.

I don't know what could possibly make this anything other than a 5-star experience. If you have the means to take this tour, it is a wonderful way to experience one of the Natural Wonders of the World.

PS. Two teens on the trip. Pretty sure the only time they used their phones for the entire day was to take photos! You know that an experience that can accomplish that is a special one!

Review Text:
This was not a bad experience - but it was a little pricey for what you get.

The hotel pick up was fine. The driver was late. I called - repeatedly. Nobody answered. I was worried that we had somehow miscommunicated. Fortunately he was just running late. But it's a little disheartening to discover that there is nobody there if a problem develops.

They pick you up super early and drive you to the little airport. We sat there waiting for about 90 minutes before we boarded the plane. That's a lot of wasted time.

The flight was fine. They have twin engine Otters (those are the ones in the pictures) and single engine Cessnas. The Otters hold about 20 and the Cessnas hold about 10 so which plane you get on depends on how many passengers are flying. I suspect that some of the flight delays might be related to consolidating trips to fill the planes.

The flight itself was fine. It felt safe enough and fun if you haven't been on a small plane before. But you wear a headset and listen to an audio recording that sounds like it was made in the 1960s. Ours started late so it wasn't synced with what we were flying over. Then it glitched and started playing the safety briefing again. Then the pilot caught on and restarted the audio - from the start - so we were now way out of sync. Then he tried to zoom forward and it was a little better. But you get the idea - it's pretty canned.

The views of the grand canyon are good. You are much lower than any commercial flight so you see the ground much better but don't get a high level perspective. It's a big loop out and back trip. Most of the people on our flight were dozing off.

Bottom line, it wasn't bad, but it wasn't something I would do again.

Review Text:
Wow! Is what comes to mind when thinking about the experience we had with Grand Canyon Landmarks Tour by Airplane. Despite a very windy day, our pilot decided it was safe enough to take us up and informed us that our flight would be rocky, but still safe. Safe was all I needed to hear.

The 45 minute flight was a tour of the entire South Rim and included an on-flight informative guide (via headphones) that turned out to be very insightful.

Finding parking at the Grand Canyon airport was fairly easy and so was our check in. I would highly recommend bringing your own camera to take pictures of what will probably be the best vantage point into the canyon. I would also try my best to board the plane first. Although everyone will get a window seat, (on a smaller plane; 8-10 people) there are a few seats that have a wing blocking your shot, thus preventing you from capturing the perfect picture. If you are simply there to take in the sights, any seat will be fine.

If you are prone to motion sickness, I would recommend bringing gum, or taking something for it before your flight departs. Keep in mind that if it is too windy and deemed unsafe your flight may be cancelled (check the weather). However, if there are high winds and it's safe to go, it will feel like a 45 minute roller-coaster ride.

I am very pleased with this experience and would definitely do it again. The ticket price is well worth it and I am very thankful that our pilot turned out to be happy and experienced and landed us safely.

Review Title: Highlight of our entire trip to the Grand Canyon
Review Text: We booked a private Ecostar Imperial helicopter tour for 6 people (the 40-50 minute flight from Grand Canyon airport in Tusayan) and we are all in agreement that this was by far the highlight of our entire trip! We checked in 30 minutes before our flight and were all weighed to distribute our weight in the helicopter evenly. We all had a good view from the big windows in the Ecostar, even the two who were in the back/middle (2 people sit next to the pilot up front, and 4 in the back), although this was probably easier because we were a family group without issues leaning over each other or asking each people closer to a window to take a photo. The weather was perfect, with little cloud cover - we chose a morning flight because we heard the light is nice and there are fewer updrafts from the hot canyon floor, making for a smoother ride, and both points were true. The pilot was excellent (Tim) and told us about various sites as we passed them and answered our questions. It was magical flying over the Kaibab forest and hitting the rim of the canyon. This was my 4th trip to the Grand Canyon but my first helicopter trip, and it was definitely an experience entirely different from walking along both rims and hiking to the base of the canyon, with panoramic views above inaccessible viewpoints. We loved seeing the full range of the Colorado River, the confluence of the Little and main Colorado River, with the color change of the water, Imperial Point at the North Rim, the view of the canyon of the North Rim without the 4.5 hour drive from the South Rim, and the Dragon Corridor. It was certainly a pricey experience, but all of us felt that it was worth every penny and we would do it again if we ever returned to the Grand Canyon!

Review Title: Det koster, men det er alle pengene værd
Review Text:
Hvis man skal til Grand Canyon National Park, bør man overveje at investere i en helikoptertur. Det koster en del, men det er det hele værd.
Der er flere udbydere, men Papillon kan bestemt anbefales.
Her er der topprofessionelle folk, der går meget op i, at det skal være en helstøbt oplevelse. Vi oplevede, at alle medarbejdere var utrolig service-mindede og høflige, og manden, der skulle hjælpe til med boarding forstod endda at joke med os gæster.
Vi blev vist hen til en af de mange helikoptere og hilste på vores venlige pilot. Han fortalte sikkert en del interessante ting undervejs, men jeg må indrømme, at når man først flyver ud over kløften - akkompagneret af temaet fra Jurassic Park i headsettet - hører man ikke meget efter.
Vores tur varede desværre kun en lille halv time, men til gengæld fik vi en oplevelse for livet.
